issues.title: [INT-01] Shared set-record and identifier contract
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer A

## Goal
Define the finished-set payload and its identifiers once. The phone, the API, Neon and Databricks all read and write the same shape.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `specs/set-record/schema.json` (JSON Schema) is the single source for the session, set, rep and flag shapes.
- [ ] TS types for that schema are exported for `apps/mobile` and `apps/api`, generated or hand-written. If hand-written, a test checks them against the schema.
- [ ] `node --test specs/*.test.mjs` covers the schema: a valid fixture passes, and fixtures missing each required field fail.
- [ ] `schema_version`, `set_index` and `rep_index` are defined in the schema. `rep_index` is 0-based within a set and matches the engine's rep numbering (AI-06).
- [ ] **Exercise ids** are the spec ids: `squat`, `push_up`, `bicep_curl`, `shoulder_press` and `lunge`. `apps/mobile/src/data/workout.ts` drops `curl` and `press`.
- [ ] **`inference_mode`** is `coreml | vision | cloud` (the phone's `PoseMode` values that can produce joints). `upload.ts` and `bronze.py` are updated from `on_device | cloud`.
- [ ] **Flag shape:** `{ rule_id, severity, rep_index }`, where `severity` is `form | safety` as in the spec schema.
- [ ] The `FinishedSession` stub in `apps/api/src/integrations/databricks/upload.ts` and the `ScoreRep` stub in `score.ts` are replaced by the shared types.
- [ ] A contract test fails when the `META_SCHEMA`, `SET`, `REP` or `FLAG` Spark schema in `databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/bronze.py` drifts from the JSON Schema.
- [ ] `docs/specs/set-record-format.md` explains each field, its unit and the clock it uses (`t_ms` since set start).

## Depends on
AI-06 (#46). This issue blocks AI-08 (#48), BE-04 (#15) and DB-04 (#4).

## Where
`specs/set-record/`, `apps/api/src/integrations/databricks/`, `databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/bronze.py`, `apps/mobile/src/data/workout.ts`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §6.1, §9.2 Workouts, §9.3 and §11.1.

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- The set record is described in three places:
  - `upload.ts` has `FinishedSession`, `FinishedSet`, `FinishedRep` and `JointFrame`, commented "mirrors the AI-08 set record".
  - `score.ts` has `ScoreRep`, with optional frame features.
  - `bronze.py` has explicit Spark schemas, commented "Keep them in sync with upload.ts".
- AI-08 (`apps/mobile/src/engine/setRecord.ts`) and DB-04 (`sets`, `reps` and `form_flags`) would each add another copy.

**Mismatches this resolves:**
- Exercise ids `curl` and `press` in the FE catalogue vs `bicep_curl` and `shoulder_press` in the specs.
- `inference_mode` is `on_device | cloud` in the uploader vs `PoseMode` on the phone. Keeping `coreml` and `vision` distinct lets the pipeline compare accuracy by pose source.
- `set_index` and `rep_index` are added only while `upload.ts` serializes, so nothing upstream knows them.

**Decision taken:** the contract lives under `specs/`, following the AI-05 pattern (schema plus a `node --test`, no install). It doesn't use a new workspace package.

**Per-frame joints:** the record keeps the flat `kp` array of 51 numbers (x, y, c for each of 17 COCO joints) and `t_ms` per frame, as `upload.ts` expects today. Only the API compresses it, so the phone never gzips anything.

**How to verify:**
- `node --test specs/*.test.mjs` passes.
- `apps/mobile` and `apps/api` both typecheck against the shared types.
- A fixture serialized by `upload.ts`'s `buildMeta` loads through `bronze.py`'s schema with an empty `_rescued_data`.

AI-06 (#46), AI-07 (#47), AI-08 (#48), FE-05 (#30), FE-06 (#31), INT-01

**Decision needed:** whether a workout is driven by today's plan (FE-09), a rehab plan (FE-16) or a free choice of exercise. The live path should accept an `exercise_id` plus effective limits, whatever chooses them.

2. Stand still for 8 s. The set ends and the rest card appears.

issues.title: [INT-03] Mobile API client, auth session and offline set queue
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** Front-end dev

## Goal
Give the app one typed API client with auth, and a persistent queue for finished sets, so a workout is saved to the server even when the phone is offline mid-set.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Client:** `apps/mobile/src/api/` has a typed client. Its base URL comes from Expo config per environment (local, a dev branch, deployed).
- [ ] **Auth:** every call sends the Neon Auth token from FE-02. A `401` clears the session and routes to login without losing queued sets.
- [ ] **Session lifecycle:** `POST /sessions`, `POST /sessions/:id/sets` and `POST /sessions/:id/finish`, using the INT-01 types.
- [ ] **Idempotent ids:** session ids and set ids are generated on the phone (UUID). A retried POST never creates a duplicate; BE-04 treats a repeated id as a no-op.
- [ ] **Queue:** finished sets and finish calls go into an MMKV-backed queue. The queue survives an app restart and replays in order when the network returns.
- [ ] **Offline set:** the set completes and the rest card shows the phone's own rule score (`phoneScore` semantics from `score.ts`). The server score and note replace it if they arrive while the rest card is still open.
- [ ] **Local store:** `apps/mobile/src/state/Training.tsx` becomes a local cache over server data, and the streak and history screens read from it. Workouts saved locally before this change are uploaded once, or left alone as a local history. Pick one and say which in the PR.
- [ ] **Sync status:** the UI never blocks on the network. A quiet "not synced yet" marker shows on a workout until its queue entries are sent.

## Depends on
BE-01 (#12), BE-02 (#13), BE-04 (#15), FE-02 (#27), INT-01

## Where
`apps/mobile/src/api/`, `apps/mobile/src/state/Training.tsx`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §3, §9.3, §14 (the phone holds only the login token) and §17 step 2 (airplane mode).

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- Nothing in `apps/mobile` calls the API.
- `Training.tsx` stores the profile and workouts in localStorage under `spotter-training-v1` on web, and only in memory on native.
- MMKV is already a dependency, used by `apps/mobile/src/pose/modeStore.ts`, with a Jest mock in `__mocks__/react-native-mmkv.ts`.

**Mismatch this resolves:** the §17 demo turns on airplane mode mid-set to show that the AI runs on the phone. Without a queue, the set POST fails and the set is lost.

**Security:** never ship Databricks or Hugging Face credentials in the app (§14). The phone reaches both only through the API.

**How to verify:**
- Jest tests cover queue order, restart persistence (with the mocked MMKV), retry with the same id, and `401` handling.
- On a device:
  1. Start a set and turn on airplane mode.
  2. Finish the set; the rest card shows the phone score.
  3. Turn airplane mode off. The set appears once in Neon.

issues.title: [INT-05] Rest-time loop: set, score, rest note and rest card in about 1.5 s
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** Back-end dev + AI engineer B

## Goal
Run the rest-time loop end to end: a finished set is scored and gets its one rest note on the rest card in about 1.5 s. The rest timer is never held up.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **One round trip:** `POST /sessions/:id/sets` saves the set, then returns `{ set_id, score, rest_note }` in the same response.
  - `score` is the `SetScore` from `scoreSet()` (CONN-05), with `source: databricks | phone`.
  - `rest_note` is `{ text, source: llm | fixed, rule_id | null }` from BE-07 and AI-11.
- [ ] **Latency budget, written down and enforced with timeouts:**
  - API save: ≤ 150 ms
  - Databricks scoring: ≤ 1200 ms (the current `DATABRICKS_SCORE_TIMEOUT_MS` default)
  - LLM rest note: ≤ 1000 ms, started as soon as the score is known
  - Total: ≤ 1.5 s typical and ≤ 2.5 s worst case. After that, the fixed note is returned.
- [ ] **Rest note content:**
  - **Clean:** "clean" follows INT-06 (rule flags only), so the note's good-news count matches the medal.
  - **Fallback:** if the LLM is slow, fails, or its output fails the banned-phrase check (`specs/banned-phrases.json`), the note is the top-priority flag's fixed `rest_note` with `{n}` and `{t}` filled in. A set with no flags gets a fixed "N of N reps were clean" line.
  - **Shape:** good news first and at most one suggestion (§7). Rule priority picks the suggestion.
- [ ] **Rest card (FE-07):** shows the note and the set medal. It shows the phone score at once, then swaps in the server result if it arrives during rest.
- [ ] **Persistence:** the score and note are saved with the set, so `GET /sets/:id/rest-note` (BE-07) returns the same text later.
- [ ] **Tests:** each fallback path has a test: Databricks timeout, Databricks 5xx, LLM timeout, banned phrase, and no flags.

## Depends on
INT-03, INT-04, INT-06, CONN-05 (#60), BE-07 (#18), AI-11 (#51), FE-07 (#32)

## Where
`apps/api/src/routes/sessions.ts`, `apps/api/src/services/restNote.ts`, `apps/mobile/src/screens/LiveSet/RestCard.tsx`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §5, §7 (the sequence diagram and phrasing table) and §18.

## Notes
**What exists today:** `score.ts` already never throws and falls back to `phoneScore()`. Its header warns that Free Edition serving endpoints scale to zero, so the first call after idle can take minutes; that is the reason for the strict timeout. `llm.ts` has timeouts and retries. BE-07 and AI-11 are open.

**Decision taken:** a single response from `POST /sets`, not a second `GET /sets/:id/rest-note` call. That saves one round trip on gym signal. BE-07's GET stays for reloading and history.

**Note wording:** the rest note must not contradict the medal. If the medal is computed from rule flags (INT-06), the note's clean count must come from the same flags.

**How to verify:**
- Run the API locally with the Databricks endpoint stopped. A set returns a phone-scored medal and the fixed note within budget.
- Start the endpoint and retry. `source` becomes `databricks`, and an LLM note is returned.
- Log the latency of each hop for 20 sets, and put the p50 and p95 in the PR.

issues.title: [INT-06] One definition of clean rep, form score and medal
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer B + Back-end dev

## Goal
Use one definition of a clean rep, the form score and the medal everywhere: the phone, the API and the Databricks pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Clean:** a rep is clean when the phone raised no rule flags for it (AI-07). Rules run with the user's injury overrides and physio limits applied (AI-16), so "clean" means "within your own limits" (§1.1, §8).
- [ ] **The model is advisory:** the Databricks form-quality model's `quality` and `label` (CONN-05, AI-10) are stored and shown, but never decide clean, form score or medal.
- [ ] **Form score:** clean reps ÷ total reps, per set and per workout.
- [ ] **Set medal, during rest:** `pickMedal` in `apps/api/src/integrations/databricks/score.ts`, fed with rule-based `clean` flags whatever the score's `source`. The model's labels no longer change the medal.
- [ ] **Workout medal, on finish:** BE-05 (`apps/api/src/services/medals.ts`). Gold means every rep clean. Silver means at or above the 4-week average form score. Otherwise bronze. A first workout is compared with a 0.70 baseline.
- [ ] **Pipeline:** `gold_workout_medals` in `databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/gold.py` uses the same definition, reading the phone's flags from `silver_reps`, not the model's quality.
- [ ] **Parity:** one shared fixture of reps (`specs/set-record/fixtures/medals/*.json`) gives the same set and workout medals in the API tests and in a pipeline test or notebook check.
- [ ] **Shown medal:** the per-set medal on the rest card (FE-07) is labelled as that set's medal. The workout medal on the summary (FE-08) comes only from BE-05.
- [ ] **Architecture:** §8 gains a short "what counts as clean" paragraph saying that rules decide and the model advises. §5's table row "Per-rep quality score, set medal" is updated to match.

## Depends on
AI-07 (#47), AI-16, BE-05 (#16), CONN-05 (#60), CONN-03 (#58)

## Where
`apps/api/src/integrations/databricks/score.ts`, `apps/api/src/services/medals.ts`, `databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/gold.py`, `specs/set-record/fixtures/medals/`, `Architecture.md` §5 and §8

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §1.1, §5, §6.3 and §8.

## Notes
**What exists today:** medals are computed in three places.
1. **`score.ts`:** `pickMedal` decides clean from the model's labels when Databricks answers, and from the phone flags only as a fallback.
2. **BE-05:** the planned workout medal service.
3. **`gold.py`:** `gold_workout_medals`.

PR #83 notes that the baseline form model "labels most reps as faults", so live scoring tends toward bronze.

**Decision taken:** rule flags decide; the model advises. This makes the medal explainable (each non-clean rep has a named rule), keeps it consistent with the amber tint the lifter saw, and keeps physio limits in force. The model's labels still feed the dashboard, `gold_training_features` and AI-10's retraining.

**Later:** once AI-10's held-out accuracy is good, this can be revisited as a single switch in one place, not three.

**How to verify:** a fixture set of 8 reps with one `knees_in` flag, where the model labels 6 reps faulty, gives a silver or bronze medal against the baseline. The API, the pipeline check and the rest card all show the same result, never a model-driven bronze.

issues.title: [INT-07] Spec, injury override and physio limit delivery to the phone
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P1 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer A + Back-end dev

## Goal
The phone always runs the right spec with the right per-user limits: the injury overrides from the user's profile and the physio limits from their rehab plan.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Spec precedence:** the bundled specs (Metro `watchFolders` on `../../specs`, loaded by `apps/mobile/src/engine/specs.ts`) work offline.
  - On launch, the app compares each `spec_version` with `GET /exercises` (BE-06) and fetches newer specs with `GET /exercises/:id/spec`.
  - A fetched spec is used only if it passes the same schema check as `specs/validate.mjs`, and it's cached in MMKV.
- [ ] **Limits endpoint:** `GET /me/limits` (BE-15) returns the user's injury body parts and active physio limits. The app caches them and refreshes them on profile or plan changes.
- [ ] **One override merge:** the phone applies injury overrides with the same merge as `applyOverride(spec, injury)` in `specs/validate.mjs`. Either both use one shared module, or a parity test runs every spec × injury combination through both and compares the outputs.
- [ ] **Order:** the effective spec is the base spec, then the injury override(s), then the physio limits (AI-16), always in that order.
- [ ] **Catalogue:** the FE exercise list (`apps/mobile/src/data/workout.ts`) comes from the spec ids and `GET /exercises`, not a hardcoded array. Names and muscles come from the library.
- [ ] **Bad server spec:** if the API returns a spec that fails validation, the bundled version is used and the failure is logged. A bad server spec never breaks a workout.

## Depends on
AI-07 (#47), AI-16, BE-03 (#14), BE-06 (#17), BE-15, INT-01

## Where
`apps/mobile/src/engine/specs.ts`, `apps/mobile/src/engine/limits.ts`, `apps/mobile/src/data/workout.ts`, `specs/validate.mjs`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §1.1, §6.2 and §9.3.

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- AI-06 bundles the five specs through `apps/mobile/metro.config.js`, which adds `path.resolve(__dirname, '../../specs')` to `watchFolders`.
- BE-06 plans to load `specs/exercises/*.json` into the `exercises.form_spec` column.
- `applyOverride` exists only in `specs/validate.mjs`.

**Open question:** AI-07 says "Injury overrides applied per user", but no issue says how the user's injuries reach the phone.

**Mismatch this resolves:** two possible copies of the override merge (the phone and the validator) and two catalogues (`workout.ts` and the specs).

**Multiple injuries:** injury overrides compose when a user has more than one injured body part. Define how, for example by applying them in a fixed body-part order with the strictest threshold winning, and add it to `docs/specs/exercise-spec-format.md`.

**How to verify:**
- A user with a knee injury squatting on the phone gets the knee target (110°).
- Change the server spec's target and relaunch. The new value is used without a rebuild.
- Break the server spec on purpose. The bundled spec is used.

issues.title: [INT-08] Session export and insights round trip
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P1 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer B + Back-end dev

## Goal
A finished workout flows from the phone to Databricks and back to the user's progress screen, for both real users and the seeded demo users.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Upload on finish:** `POST /sessions/:id/finish` queues the CONN-02 upload. `sessions.export_status` goes `pending → uploading → exported` (or `failed`, with `export_error`).

- [ ] **Sync:** `syncInsights` (CONN-06) upserts into `progress_daily` and `risk_insights` in Neon, which DB-07 creates.
- [ ] **Read path:** `GET /me/progress` and `GET /me/insights` (BE-13) return the new data. FE-14 shows it.
- [ ] **Demo users:** they're created so their Databricks ids are the HMAC pseudonyms (`pseudonymize()` in `upload.ts`) of seeded Neon users. The DB-10 seed and the synthetic-data notebook share one list of seed user ids.
- [ ] **Runbook:** `docs/runbooks/session-roundtrip.md` covers how to trigger the pipeline by hand, the sync interval, and where to look when a session doesn't show up.

## Depends on
INT-04, CONN-02 (#57), CONN-03 (#58), CONN-06 (#61), DB-07 (#7), DB-10 (#10), BE-13 (#24), FE-14 (#39)

## Where
`apps/api/src/routes/sessions.ts`, `apps/api/src/jobs/`, `apps/api/scripts/seed-demo.ts`, `databricks/notebooks/`, `docs/runbooks/`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §9.1, §11.1, §11.3 and §13.

## Notes
**What exists today:** CONN-02, 03 and 06 are closed, with code on `main`:
- `upload.ts`
- `databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/{bronze,silver,gold}.py`
- `syncInsights.ts`

The pieces have only been tested apart. PR #83 notes:

- `progress_daily` is written by the sync, but DB-07 doesn't define it. DB-07 is being updated to own it.

**Out of scope:** account deletion (§13) is owned by CONN-13.

**How to verify:**

2. Run the pipeline and wait for one sync, or trigger it by hand.
3. The progress screen shows that day's reps and form score.

issues.title: [INT-09] End-to-end replay test on recorded clips, plus CI
issues.body:
**Area:** integration · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer A

## Goal
One command replays recorded joint clips through the whole phone-to-API path and checks the results against golden outputs, so a change in any area that breaks another shows up before the demo.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Recordings:** at least one clean clip and one off-form clip per exercise with a recording, captured on a phone with the `PoseDebugScreen` recorder in AI-06's `Clip` format (`apps/mobile/src/engine/recording.ts`). They're stored as fixtures.
- [ ] **Each clip's `expected` lists:**
  - reps
  - partials
  - set end

- [ ] **Phone half:** a harness replays a clip through:
  1. `createFormEngine` (AI-06)
  2. the rules (AI-07)
  3. the set record (AI-08)

  It compares the counts, the flags and a snapshot of the INT-01 payload.
- [ ] **API half:** a harness posts that payload to the API, running locally against PGlite or a throwaway Neon branch. Databricks and Hugging Face are mocked at the HTTP boundary.
  - It checks the stored `sets`, `reps` and `form_flags` rows.
  - It checks the medal (INT-06).
  - It checks the rest-note fallback.
  - It checks the upload payload `upload.ts` would send.
- [ ] **Commands:** `npm run test:e2e` at the repo root, or one documented command per app, runs both halves.
- [ ] **CI:** a GitHub Actions workflow runs `node --test specs/*.test.mjs`, the mobile Jest suite and this harness on every PR. The repo has no CI today.

## Depends on
INT-01, INT-04, AI-06 (#46), AI-07 (#47), AI-08 (#48), BE-04 (#15)

## Where
`apps/mobile/src/engine/__fixtures__/`, `tests/e2e/`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §6.1 and §16 (the "Integration + bug bash" block).

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- **Synthetic clips:** AI-06 ships a generator (`apps/mobile/src/engine/__fixtures__/synth.ts`), a loader and the clip format with `source: 'synthetic' | 'recorded'`.
- **Real clips:** AI-06's own criterion, "no double counts on a recorded test clip", needs a real recording. This issue supplies it for every exercise.

- rules → payload (`rep_index`)

**Privacy:** recorded clips are joints only (§13), and everyone filmed must consent, as AI-09 requires.

issues.title: [DB-12] Schema: rehab plans, physio limits and range-of-motion trend
issues.body:
**Area:** database · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** Back-end dev

## Goal
Add tables for the plan a physio gave the user, its per-exercise limits, and the synced range-of-motion trend.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `rehab_plans`:
  - `id`, `user_id`, `injury_id` (nullable FK to `injuries`), `from_physio` (free text, such as the clinic or physio name the user enters)
  - `start_on`, `review_on`, `status` (`active | paused | done`), `notes`, `created_at`
- [ ] `rehab_limits`:
  - `id`, `rehab_plan_id`, `exercise_id` (a spec id), `angle` (a spec angle name such as `knee` or `elbow`), `side` (`left | right | both`)
  - `max_range_deg`, `sets`, `reps`, `tempo_min_ms` (nullable)
- [ ] `injuries` gains `side` (`left | right | both | n/a`), so range-of-motion trends can compare the injured side with the healthy side.
- [ ] `rom_trend` holds the Neon copy of `gold_rom_trend`:
  - **Columns:** `user_id`, `angle`, `side`, `week`, `peak_range_deg`, `baseline_range_deg`, `healthy_side_range_deg`, `change_deg`, `synced_at`
  - **Upsert key:** (`user_id`, `angle`, `side`, `week`)
- [ ] Every table cascades on user delete. Rehab data is private by default (§13), and there's no public read path.
- [ ] The migration applies cleanly on a fresh branch.

## Depends on
DB-03 (#3), DB-05 (#5)

## Where
`apps/api/drizzle/schema/rehab.ts`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §1.1 (the recovery feature table), §9.2 Planning (`REHAB_PLAN`, `REHAB_LIMIT`) and §13.

## Notes
**What exists today:** Architecture §9.2 already draws `REHAB_PLAN { id, from_physio, start, review_on }` and `REHAB_LIMIT { exercise_id, joint, max_range_deg, sets, reps }`, but no issue creates them. Before this issue, `issues/issues.json` had no rehab or physio issues.

**Why `angle` rather than `joint`:** limits are stored against a spec angle name (`knee`, `elbow`, `trunk`), not a COCO joint. That's what the form engine measures, so AI-16 can apply a limit without guessing which angle a joint means. `max_range_deg` is flexion from straight (180° − the joint angle), which is how physios state range.

**Related issues:**
- The sync side of `rom_trend` is CONN-14.
- The read side is BE-16.

issues.title: [BE-17] Back-to-gym milestone
issues.body:
**Area:** backend · **Priority:** P1 · **Suggested owner:** Back-end dev + AI engineer B

## Goal
Suggest moving from the rehab plan to a regular gym plan when the user's range and form have been steady at the physio's targets. The user always confirms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Rule:** `apps/api/src/services/milestone.ts` checks `rom_trend` and the medal history. Suggested defaults, kept in one config object:
  - range within 5° of the physio's target, or of the healthy side, for 2 consecutive weeks
  - at least 3 silver or gold workouts on the rehab plan's exercises in the last 2 weeks
  - no `physio_limit` flags in the last week
- [ ] **Endpoint:** `GET /me/milestones` returns a pending suggestion with its reasons, such as "knee range has held at 118° for 2 weeks".
- [ ] **Accept or dismiss:** `POST /me/milestones/:id/accept` marks the rehab plan `done` and offers plan generation (BE-08). `POST /me/milestones/:id/dismiss` hides the suggestion for 2 weeks.
- [ ] **Wording:** the suggestion always says to check with the physio first (§1.1), and it never changes or removes limits by itself.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit tests cover a user who qualifies, a user one week short, and a user with a recent `physio_limit` flag.

## Depends on
BE-05 (#16), BE-15, BE-16, CONN-14

## Where
`apps/api/src/services/milestone.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/recovery.ts`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §1.1 ("Back-to-gym milestone") and §8.

## Notes
- The thresholds are heuristics, not medical criteria. Say so in the code and in the response, and keep them easy to tune.
- When a suggestion is accepted, an optional opt-in feed post ("Back to the gym!") can reuse BE-10. It's never automatic.

issues.title: [AI-16] Physio limits in the form engine
issues.body:
**Area:** ai · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer A

## Goal
Apply each user's physio limits in the form engine and the rules, on top of the injury overrides, so that "clean" means "within what my physio allowed".

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **`applyRehabLimits(spec, limits)`** in `apps/mobile/src/engine/limits.ts` returns the effective spec. It runs after the injury overrides (`applyOverride`) and is pure, with no side effects.
- [ ] **Mapping for a `joint_angle` primary with `direction: "decreasing"`:**
  - A limit of `max_range_deg` on that angle gives an allowed minimum angle of 180 − `max_range_deg`.
  - `target` moves to at least that value, so the depth or range rule never asks for more than the physio allows.
  - If `count_min` would fall below it, `count_min` is raised so the threshold order (`start_enter > start_exit > count_min ≥ target`) still holds.
- [ ] **`direction: "increasing"`** (shoulder press): either define the mapping, or reject the limit with a clear validation error. Document whichever is chosen.
- [ ] **New safety rule:** a generated rule `physio_limit` (severity `safety`, phase `rep`, check `min ≥ allowed minimum`) flags any rep that goes past the prescribed range. The flag is held until the set ends like any other (§7). The physio report (BE-16) counts these flags.
- [ ] **Tempo:** `tempo_min_ms` patches the spec's tempo rule value when it's stricter.
- [ ] **Validation:** the effective spec passes the same checks as `specs/validate.mjs`: threshold order, references, and note tone. A limit that can't be applied is reported back, never silently ignored.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit tests cover a knee limit on `squat` and `lunge`, an elbow limit on `bicep_curl`, a limit stacked on the `knee` injury override, and an impossible limit.
- [ ] **Docs:** `docs/specs/exercise-spec-format.md` gains a "Physio limits" section, and Architecture §6.2's last bullet points to it.

## Depends on
AI-07 (#47), BE-15, DB-12

## Where
`apps/mobile/src/engine/limits.ts`, `docs/specs/exercise-spec-format.md`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §1.1 ("Plan from my physio") and §6.2 ("A physio's own limits (`REHAB_LIMIT`) are applied per user, on top").

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- Injury overrides are fixed per body part in each spec, with `applyOverride` in `specs/validate.mjs`.
- Architecture says physio limits apply "on top", but no issue implements them.

**What depends on this:**
- INT-06 (clean is judged against the user's own limits).
- INT-07 (delivering the limits to the phone).
- BE-16 (counting reps outside the limits).

**The demo needs it:** §17 step 5 says "The same squat set, judged against the physio's limits, earns gold".

**Spec format:** if `physio_limit` needs a new `label` for the §6.3 model label list, update the label list in the spec schema and validator together, following the AI-05 change rules.

issues.title: [CONN-13] Account deletion: Neon cascade and Databricks delete job
issues.body:
**Area:** connections · **Priority:** P1 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer B + Back-end dev

## Goal
When a user deletes their account, remove their data from Neon and from Databricks, as Architecture §13 promises.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `DELETE /me` cascades in Neon: users, profiles, injuries, rehab plans, sessions, sets, reps, flags, posts, comments, kudos, follows, buddy matches, `progress_daily`, `risk_insights` and `rom_trend`.
- [ ] Before the user row goes, the API writes the user's pseudonym (`pseudonymize()` from `apps/api/src/integrations/databricks/upload.ts`) to a `deletion_requests` table. That table holds no other personal data.
- [ ] A Databricks job (`databricks/notebooks/delete_user.py`, scheduled daily or triggered by the API) reads pending requests and deletes every row for that pseudonym:
  - all bronze, silver and gold tables
  - the uploaded files under `/Volumes/spotter/raw/sessions/{meta,joints}/`
  - the MLflow training feature table
- [ ] The job marks each request `done` with a timestamp. A failed run retries, and deleting twice is harmless.
- [ ] Gold tables and the dashboards no longer show the user after the next pipeline run. The insight sync skips unknown pseudonyms, as it already does.
- [ ] Published Hub datasets (CONN-12) contain only the team's consenting clips (§6.3), so they need no deletion. The runbook says so explicitly.
- [ ] `docs/runbooks/account-deletion.md` describes the flow and how to check it worked.

## Depends on
CONN-01 (#56), CONN-03 (#58), BE-02 (#13), DB-04 (#4), DB-07 (#7)

## Where
`apps/api/src/routes/me.ts`, `apps/api/drizzle/schema/`, `databricks/notebooks/delete_user.py`, `docs/runbooks/account-deletion.md`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §13 ("Account deletion cascades in Neon and queues a delete job in Databricks").

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- `upload.ts` line 128 already mentions "The Databricks delete job (§13)", but no issue owns it.
- `syncInsights.ts` skips rows for unknown pseudonyms, which covers deleted accounts on the Neon side.

**Why a request table:** the HMAC pseudonym can't be recomputed after the user row is gone, so it must be captured first. Store only the pseudonym and a timestamp.

**Delta tables:** a delete followed by `VACUUM` actually removes the old files. Check what Free Edition allows, and note the retention window in the runbook.

issues.title: [CONN-14] gold_rom_trend pipeline table and Neon sync
issues.body:
**Area:** connections · **Priority:** P0 · **Suggested owner:** AI engineer B

## Goal
Build `gold_rom_trend`: each user's weekly range of motion per joint and side, compared with their injured-side baseline and their healthy side, and synced into Neon.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `gold_rom_trend` in `databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/gold.py`:
  - **Columns:** `user_id`, `angle`, `side`, `week`, `peak_range_deg`, `baseline_range_deg`, `healthy_side_range_deg`, `change_deg`
  - **Source:** `silver_reps` (`left_range_deg`, `right_range_deg`)
  - **Peak range:** a robust peak per week, such as the 90th percentile of rep range, so one bad frame doesn't spike it.
- [ ] **Baseline:** the injured-side baseline is the first two weeks of data after the rehab plan's `start_on`, or the first two weeks of data if there's no plan.
- [ ] **Injured side:** it comes from the session's injury info. CONN-02's `injury_groups` gains a coarse side, without dates or notes (§13).
- [ ] **Sync:** `syncInsights` (CONN-06) gains a third mapping, `gold_rom_trend` → `rom_trend` (DB-12), with the same idempotent upsert pattern.
- [ ] **Synthetic data:** the synthetic-data notebook produces believable recovery curves, for example knee range up about 18° over three weeks (the §17 line), for the seeded demo users.
- [ ] **Expectations:** the pipeline rejects a range outside 0–180° and a week with fewer than 3 reps.

## Depends on
CONN-03 (#58), CONN-06 (#61), DB-12, INT-01

## Where
`databricks/pipelines/spotter_sessions/gold.py`, `apps/api/src/jobs/syncInsights.ts`, `databricks/notebooks/`

## Context
See `Architecture.md` §1.1 ("Range-of-motion tracking"), §11.1 (the `gold_rom_trend` row) and §17 step 5.

## Notes
**What exists today:**
- Architecture §11.1 lists `gold_rom_trend`, but `gold.py` doesn't build it.
- `silver.py` already computes `left_range_deg` and `right_range_deg` per rep from the primary angle, so the inputs exist.

**Range definition:** range is measured on the spec's primary angle per rep. Some exercises measure a different joint than the injured one; a shoulder injury doing squats is one example. Only emit a trend for an angle when the exercise's primary angle matches the injured joint, and list that mapping in the code.

**Wording:** this is a trend, not a diagnosis (§11.2). Column names and comments should read that way too.
